phases.title: Plan and decide
phases.summary: Settle the question, the route and who does what before anything is submitted.

phases.title: Authorise and notify
phases.summary: Get permission to start, and keep the authorities told of changes.

phases.title: Build and activate
phases.summary: Systems, providers, sites, supplies and training made ready, in parallel.

phases.title: Conduct
phases.summary: Enrol, collect data and report safety. Version 1 shows the safety and notification clocks only.

phases.title: Close and report
phases.summary: End the study, report results, lock the data. Version 1 shows the notification clocks and the lock.

phases.title: Archive
phases.summary: Keep the record for as long as the rules say, and close out providers.

changelog.text: Version 1 published: phases 1 to 3 in full, and the safety, notification and archive clocks for phases 4 to 6.

Coordinated assessment under MDR Article 78(14) is shown as the consolidated text of 10 January 2025 reads, as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2024/1860. An earlier working note gave a fixed date of 27 May 2027, which that text does not carry; it is not used.
Device safety-reporting day counts, the development safety update report due date and drug-trial modification day counts are marked Not shown: they were not read at the primary text.
Service-provider responsibility and oversight are cited to ICH E6(R3) sections 3.6 and 3.9.5.

steps.title: Decide which rules the study sits under
steps.settle: Whether the study is a clinical trial of a medicinal product, a clinical investigation of a device, or a combined study, and so which set of rules, forms and clocks applies. Who makes that decision and who records it.
steps.leaves: A short written route decision with its reasons, dated and signed off by the accountable person, kept in the study file.

notes.text: This map does not classify any study. When the route is unclear, the authority's own guidance and the authority itself decide.

steps.title: Fix the endpoints and how each is assessed
steps.settle: What will be measured, when, and by whom or on what. Which assessments are clinician-reported, patient-reported, observer-reported or performance-based, and whether any instrument needs a licence or a translation.
steps.leaves: A schedule of assessments tied to the protocol objectives, with each instrument's type, languages and licence state noted.

steps.title: Ask patients about the material and the burden
steps.settle: Whether patients or their representatives review the participant information, the consent material and the burden of the visit schedule before they are final, and how their comments are handled.
steps.leaves: A record of what was asked, what changed because of it and what did not, and why.

steps.title: Name the sponsor and any legal representative
steps.settle: Who the sponsor is, where it is established, and whether a legal representative or a contact person in the Union is needed.
steps.leaves: A named sponsor and, where the rule applies, a named representative with a written scope of what they answer for.
owners: Legal representative, where one is needed

facts.label: Sponsor not established in the Union

steps.title: Decide what goes to providers and choose them
steps.settle: Which activities are handed to a contract research organisation or another provider, how providers are assessed and chosen, and what stays with the sponsor.
steps.leaves: A list of the activities handed over, a selection record, and a written agreement in place before those activities start.

steps.title: Choose sites that can run the study
steps.settle: Which sites can recruit the population, run the procedures and keep the records the protocol needs, and what each site said it could and could not do.
steps.leaves: A site list with the reason each site was chosen and the feasibility answers each one gave.

steps.title: Agree the budget and the contracts
steps.settle: Who pays for what, how a change is priced, and who signs for the sponsor, each site and each provider.
steps.leaves: Signed agreements and a budget with a rule for changes. Each contract names the activities it covers.

steps.title: Plan start-up as parallel streams
steps.settle: Which streams run at the same time (authorisation, contracts, systems, supply, site readiness), which one sets the date of the first subject in, and who watches that stream.
steps.leaves: A start-up plan that shows each stream, its owner and what it is waiting for, revised at each stage.

notes.text: This is a ClinicOps reading of how start-up work is organised, not a rule from any regulator. No duration is shown for any stream.

steps.title: Submit the initial application in CTIS
steps.settle: What goes into Part I and Part II, who prepares each part, and what the Member State is likely to ask.
steps.leaves: A submitted application with its dossier and a dated timeline of the statutory periods.

facts.label: Initial application
facts.figure: Validation 10 days; Part I 45 days; Part II 45 days; decision within 5 days of the later of the two

steps.title: Apply for the clinical investigation
steps.settle: Which application route applies, who prepares the documentation, and how changes to it will be notified.
steps.leaves: A submitted application, a validation date and, for investigations that need authorisation, an authorisation decision.

facts.label: Application and authorisation
facts.figure: Validation notice within 10 days; sponsor response up to 10 days, extendable by 20; authorisation within 45 days of validation, extendable by 20

not_shown.text: National additions, ethics committee steps and fees are not shown. Read the Member State authority's current page.

steps.title: Notify a post-market clinical follow-up investigation
steps.settle: Whether the investigation adds procedures that are invasive or burdensome, and who sends the notification and when.
steps.leaves: A notification sent before the investigation starts, with the date recorded.

facts.label: Notification before commencement
facts.figure: At least 30 days before the investigation starts

steps.title: Check whether coordinated assessment applies
steps.settle: Whether the investigation will be conducted in more than one Member State and whether those Member States have agreed to apply the coordinated assessment procedure.
steps.leaves: A note of which Member States apply the procedure to this investigation, and the basis for that note.

facts.label: Who must apply the procedure, and from when

not_shown.text: No date for mandatory use is shown. It is counted from a Commission notice that was not found, so it cannot be worked out.

steps.title: Check the EUDAMED module status for clinical investigations
steps.settle: Whether the module for clinical investigations has been declared functional and mandatory, because that changes where and how an application or a notification is made.
steps.leaves: A dated note of the module status and where it was read, refreshed before each submission.

facts.label: Module status as the Commission states it

steps.title: Cover ethics review and national requirements
steps.settle: Which ethics body or bodies review, which national or local documents, languages and fees apply in each country, and who submits each item.
steps.leaves: A country-by-country list of submissions, owners and dates.

not_shown.text: No national day counts, fees or language rules are shown on this map. Read the authority's current page for each country.

steps.title: Authorise a substantial modification
steps.settle: Whether a change to the protocol or the dossier needs authorisation before it is applied, and who assesses it.
steps.leaves: A change log and, where needed, an authorised modification before the change is used.

not_shown.text: No figure shown: not verified at primary source. The day counts for authorising a substantial modification were not read in this version.

steps.title: Notify a substantial modification
steps.settle: Whether a change is likely to have a substantial impact on the safety, health or rights of subjects or on the data, and who decides that.
steps.leaves: A notification with the reasons and nature of the change, and a record of the earliest date it may be put into use.

facts.label: Notification and earliest implementation
facts.figure: Notify within one week; implement at the earliest 38 days after notification, extendable by seven days

steps.title: Activate each site
steps.settle: What each site must have before its first subject: approvals received, agreements signed, staff trained and assigned their duties, supplies and systems available.
steps.leaves: A site activation record per site, showing the date each requirement was met and who confirmed it.

steps.title: Train the study team
steps.settle: Who needs training on the protocol, the systems, the safety reporting duties and the procedures, and how completion is recorded.
steps.leaves: Training records linked to each person's role, and a plan for retraining when the protocol or a system changes.

steps.title: Secure licences and language versions for assessments
steps.settle: Whether each instrument may be used electronically in each language, and for each language whether an approved version exists or a new translation is needed, with a rule for who signs off wording.
steps.leaves: A licence request per instrument, a translation route per language, and a record of the wording that was signed off.

not_shown.text: No licensing or translation duration is shown. Durations vary by instrument and owner; the lead-time planner works from your own numbers.

links.label: COA in Denmark and the Nordics

steps.title: Build and test the study systems
steps.settle: That the data capture and eCOA systems collect what the protocol says, are tested against written requirements before use, and have a change control route once live.
steps.leaves: Written requirements, a test record signed off on the sponsor side, and a change log that stays open through the study.

steps.title: Plan how providers will be overseen
steps.settle: What is reviewed for each provider, how often, who acts on findings, and how the plan changes with the risk of the activity.
steps.leaves: An oversight plan, a meeting and issue log, and an escalation route that the provider has seen.

facts.label: Oversight fit for purpose and tailored to risk

steps.title: Get supplies to sites
steps.settle: That the investigational product or device, comparators and ancillary supplies are available at each site, with the storage and accountability records the protocol needs.
steps.leaves: A supply plan, a release record for each shipment and a way for a site to report a problem.

steps.title: Write the safety management plan
steps.settle: Who receives safety information at the site and at the sponsor and in what form, how fast it is assessed, who decides expectedness and causality, how reports reach the authorities and the sites, and who covers out-of-hours.
steps.leaves: A plan that names each role, each channel and each clock listed in the Conduct phase, with the training and the reconciliation routine behind it.

notes.text: The clocks themselves are in the safety steps of the Conduct phase, each with its own source.

steps.title: Set up the master file
steps.settle: Where the study's essential documents will be kept, who files them, and how completeness is checked as the study runs.
steps.leaves: A file structure and filing rules agreed with each provider, and a first completeness check date.

steps.title: Take the go decision for the first subject
steps.settle: Each stream confirms its requirements are met, and one named person records the decision to start.
steps.leaves: A dated go record that lists each stream's confirmation and any open item that was accepted, with the reason.

steps.title: Notify start, first visit and end of recruitment
steps.settle: Who sends each notification, from which date each period runs in each Member State, and what a restart of recruitment triggers.
steps.leaves: Three dated notifications per Member State, each matched to the event it reports.

facts.label: Start; first visit of the first subject; end of recruitment
facts.figure: Each within 15 days of the event

steps.title: Investigator reports a serious adverse event to the sponsor
steps.settle: That every site knows how to report, to whom, in what form, and which events the protocol says need no immediate report.
steps.leaves: A dated report from the investigator for each serious event and a record of when the sponsor received it.

facts.label: Investigator to sponsor
facts.figure: Within 24 hours of obtaining knowledge, unless the protocol provides otherwise for certain events

steps.title: Report suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions
steps.settle: Who assesses seriousness, expectedness and causality, on which reference safety information, and who submits the report.
steps.leaves: A dated submission for each reaction, the assessment behind it and the date the sponsor became aware.

facts.label: Fatal or life-threatening
facts.figure: As soon as possible and not later than 7 days after the sponsor became aware

facts.label: Other reactions
facts.figure: Not later than 15 days after the sponsor became aware

facts.label: First not fatal, later proved fatal or life-threatening
facts.figure: Not later than 7 days after the sponsor became aware that it was fatal or life-threatening

steps.title: Report adverse events and device deficiencies in a device investigation
steps.settle: Which events the investigator reports to the sponsor, which the sponsor reports to the Member States, in what form, and how the sponsor decides a causal relationship.
steps.leaves: A dated record of each event, who assessed it, and when each report was sent.

facts.label: Sponsor reports to Member States without delay

not_shown.text: No figure shown: not verified at primary source. The investigator-to-sponsor and sponsor-to-Member-State day counts used in practice come from MDCG 2020-10/1, which was not opened for this version.

steps.title: Report other unexpected events that affect benefit and risk
steps.settle: Who watches for events that are not suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions but change the benefit-risk balance, and who decides to report.
steps.leaves: A dated notification and the reasoning for it.

facts.label: Notification to Member States
facts.figure: Without undue delay and no later than 15 days from the date the sponsor became aware

steps.title: Take and notify urgent safety measures
steps.settle: Who may decide on a measure at short notice, how the investigators are told, and who notifies the Member States.
steps.leaves: A record of the event, the measures taken and the date each was taken, with the notification.

facts.label: Notification to Member States
facts.figure: Without undue delay and no later than 7 days from the date the measures have been taken

steps.title: Notify a serious breach
steps.settle: Who can raise a suspected breach, who decides whether it is serious, and who notifies the Member States.
steps.leaves: A breach record with the date the sponsor became aware, the decision and its reasons, and the notification.

facts.label: Notification to Member States
facts.figure: Without undue delay and not later than 7 days of becoming aware of the breach

steps.title: Submit the annual safety report
steps.settle: Which investigational products need a report, which period it covers, and who compiles and submits it.
steps.leaves: A submitted report for each product, with aggregate and anonymised data.

facts.label: Annual report per investigational product other than placebo

not_shown.text: No due date is shown for a development safety update report. No figure shown: not verified at primary source, and how it serves as this report was not read.

steps.title: Notify a halt or early termination
steps.settle: Who can decide to halt, how sites and participants are told, who notifies the authorities, and what is needed before a restart.
steps.leaves: A dated decision with its reasons, the notifications sent and, before any restart, a record of what was authorised.

facts.label: Halt or early termination for subject safety
facts.figure: Without undue delay and not later than 15 days of the date of the halt or termination

facts.label: Temporary halt or early termination
facts.figure: Within 15 days, with a justification; within 24 hours to all Member States where it was on safety grounds

steps.title: Notify the end of the study
steps.settle: When the study ends, who fixes that date against the protocol, and who sends each notification.
steps.leaves: A recorded end date with its basis, and the notifications for each Member State.

facts.label: End of the trial
facts.figure: Within 15 days of the end in each Member State concerned, and within 15 days of the end in the last Member State and third country

facts.label: End of the investigation
facts.figure: Within 15 days of the end in each Member State, and within 15 days of the end in all of them; the end is the last visit of the last subject unless the plan says otherwise

steps.title: Submit the results summary or report
steps.settle: What the summary or report contains, who writes the lay summary, and what the protocol says when results cannot be ready in time.
steps.leaves: A submitted summary and, for devices, a report, each with the date of the end it is counted from.

facts.label: Results summary
facts.figure: Within one year from the end of the trial in all Member States concerned, with a lay summary

facts.label: Clinical investigation report and summary
facts.figure: Within one year of the end, or within three months of an early termination or temporary halt

steps.title: Submit the clinical study report for a marketing authorisation
steps.settle: Whether the trial was intended to support a marketing authorisation, and which party is the applicant that submits the report.
steps.leaves: A submitted clinical study report with a note of the event it was counted from.

facts.label: Clinical study report
facts.figure: Within 30 days after the marketing authorisation is granted, the procedure is completed or the application is withdrawn

steps.title: Reconcile and lock the data
steps.settle: That the data are complete and cleaned, that the clinical and safety databases agree, that open queries and protocol deviations are resolved or accepted, and who authorises the lock.
steps.leaves: A lock record, a reconciliation record and a list of the open items that were accepted, with reasons.

steps.title: Archive the study record
steps.settle: What goes into the archive, who holds it, who may open it, and how it stays readable for the whole period.
steps.leaves: An archive index, named archive holders and an access record, with the date the period started.

facts.label: Master file archiving
facts.figure: At least 25 years after the end of the trial, unless other Union law requires longer

not_shown.text: No figure shown: not verified at primary source. The archiving period for a device investigation was not read in this version.

steps.title: Close out each provider
steps.settle: What each provider hands back or transfers (data, documents, system access), what is deleted, and how the sponsor confirms it.
steps.leaves: A close-out checklist per provider and a signed handover record.
